maria: Heads-up: added a tiny Next.js sample that demonstrates Redwood SDK + LlamaIndex wiring for a simple RAG flow. Repo link (internal): https://git.redwood.local/next-sample-rag
josh: sweet. any special setup steps?
maria: npm install, copy .env.example to .env.local, set REDWOOD_HOST and REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the cookie-based dev auth helper. Starts on :3000.
josh: I tried it and embeddings/generate calls work, but the sample eval page shows empty results intermittently. Browser devtools show 401s hitting /v1/events.
maria: that's odd. The sample uses an API route proxy at /api/redwood that forwards requests to REDWOOD_HOST. snippet: ```export default async (req,res)=>{ const r = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_HOST + req.url, {method:req.method, headers:{'content-type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(req.body)}); res.status(r.status).send(await r.text()); }```
ara: missing auth forward. When running locally with the dev auth cookie the browser doesn't set Authorization header, so the proxy must forward cookie header upstream or add Authorization from env.
josh: yep. also noticed different retry behavior compared to our Node SDK: the browser helper returns 429 directly while the server SDK retries. That causes the sample UI to fail under quick reloads.
maria: I think we should: 1) update the proxy to forward Authorization and cookies; 2) add a small client-side retry utility to mimic server SDK backoff; 3) include a lightweight eval harness script for maintainers.
toby: for retries we usually use jittered exponential backoff. simple helper idea:
```js
async function fetchWithBackoff(url, opts, retries=4){
  for(let i=0;i<retries;i++){
    const res = await fetch(url, opts)
    if(res.status !== 429) return res
    const delay = Math.min(1000, 200 * Math.pow(2, i)) + Math.round(Math.random()*100)
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, delay))
  }
  return fetch(url, opts)
}
```
ara: also added sample cache wrapper in the starter earlier; it used indefinite keys for quick debugging. For repeated evals that's causing local memory pressure. We should give a default TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) in the sample to avoid leaks.
josh: agree. can be an opt-out in env (CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=0 for no expiry).
maria: I'll open a PR that includes: proxy auth forwarding, fetchWithBackoff in client utils, scripts/eval-harness.js which can run N parallel requests and optionally POST to MOCK_TELEMETRY_URL, README updates.
